newsitem.title: USA: Plains direct cattle trade steady at $72 -feedlots.
newsitem.headline: Plains direct cattle trade steady at $72 -feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains direct cattle markets Tuesday were steady in light trading, feedlot sources said.

About 2,000 head sold at $72.00 per cwt in the Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma area, steady with Monday's light volume and unchanged from last week's top price, the sources and USDA said. Kansas feedlots sold about 600 head at $72.00, sources there said.
Further bids at $72.00 were countered by asking levels of $74.00 for the bulk of cattle in this week's showlist, which was estimated smaller than last weeks, sources said.
Cattle prices also were expected to be underpinned this week by strong beef demand, but mixed boxed beef values at midday Tuesday suggested that retail interest for choice cuts was starting to waver.
Boxed beef prices at midday were quoted down $0.30 to $0.41 per cwt for choice, yield-grade 1 to 3 cuts but up $0.35 to $0.38 for select grades, according to USDA.

Demand for beef Monday was active at higher prices and fueled ideas that retailers were restocking coolers after strong weekend beef clearance. But demand appeared to be slowing Tuesday as retailers have done the fill-in purchasing, the sources said.
